question: The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change notified the E-Waste Management Rules in 2022. These rules are supposed to come into force from __________.
solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**1 April 2023**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The E-Waste Management Rules notified by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change will come into force from April 1, 2023.**
 
• These rules are aimed at regulating the management of e-waste, which is a major environmental hazard due to the presence of** **toxic substances.
 
• The rules mandate the producers of electronic products to **collect and dispose** of e-waste in an environmentally sound manner.
 
• The rules also require the establishment of** **collection centers**, **dismantling and recycling facilities, and the adoption of best practices for handling e-waste.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India ranks fifth globally in terms of generating e-waste.**
 
• **2016's **New E-Waste Management Regulations:
 
 
• **Compact fluorescent bulbs, or CFL**s, as well as other mercury-containing lamps and related equipment, are included.
 
• **For the first time, producers are included in the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework together with the targets thanks to the Rules.**
 
• Producers are now responsible for both the exchange and collection of e-waste.
 
• **Manufacturers, dealers, refurbishers, and Producer Responsibility Organizations are among the other parties involved.**
 
• The regulations now cover Compact Fluorescent bulbs (**CFLs) and other bulbs** that contain mercury.
